cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Synapse – a junction between two nerve cells in the brain.

p.em: Example: Signals travel across the synapse to connect brain cells.

cosy-blockquote.p: Artificial ≠ Natural – made or produced by human beings rather than occurring naturally ≠ existing in or caused by nature; not made or caused by humankind.

p.em: Example: There is a massive contrast between artificial networks and natural biological brains.

cosy-blockquote.p: Contrast – the state of being strikingly different from something else.

p.em: Example: There is a massive contrast between biological and digital brains.

cosy-blockquote.p: Network – a complex system of interconnected things, cells, or computers.

p.em: Example: Our brain is a vast biological network of billions of cells.

cosy-blockquote.p: Energy – power derived from physical or chemical resources.

p.em: Example: The brain uses very little energy to perform complex calculations.

cosy-blockquote.p: Plasticity – the brain's ability to adapt and change its structure.

p.em: Example: Synaptic plasticity is the biological basis of learning.

cosy-blockquote.p: Node – a connection point in a system or artificial network.

p.em: Example: An artificial neural network consists of thousands of nodes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Efficiency ≠ Inefficiency – the state or quality of being efficient and saving resources ≠ lack of efficiency; waste of time or energy.

p.em: Example: Biological brains possess superior energy efficiency, whereas standard digital chips show thermodynamic inefficiency.

cosy-blockquote.p: Structure – the arrangement of and relations between parts of something.

p.em: Example: The brain's structure is fundamentally different from a chip.

cosy-blockquote.p: Compare – estimate, measure, or note the similarity or dissimilarity.

p.em: Example: Scientists compare artificial nodes to biological synapses.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
According to the article, how does a biological synapse pass signals, and what makes it superior to a computer?
★ Have you ever wondered how your brain remembers things from your early childhood?

What evidence presented in the study highlights why artificial intelligence uses different principles to process information?
★ When did you first interact with an AI chatbot, and what was your impression?

How does the article contrast the human brain with a microchip's structural layout?
★ Do you prefer reading paper books or using digital screens for studying?

According to the research, how does the brain's network of cells adapt when we acquire a new skill?
★ What physical skill or sport did you find hardest to learn in your life?

What empirical findings in the study show that human brains require very little energy compared to AI?
★ What is your favorite food or drink to recharge your brain after a hard day of work?

How does the article describe the role of biological plasticity during continuous learning?
★ Have you ever had to change a strong daily habit, and how difficult was it?

According to the article, how does a standard AI node differ from a biological neuron?
★ Do you consider yourself a person who likes to understand how machines work?

What specific evidence does the article present to show the brain's superior efficiency?
★ What is your most productive time of the day to study or work?

How does the article show that the physical structure of the brain supports sparse coding?
★ Do you rely more on logic or gut feelings when making major life choices?

When scientists compare an AI's backpropagation with brain learning, what core differences do they highlight?
★ Have you ever created any art, music, or writing that you felt proud of?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
If future research continues to support this study, how will bio-computing chips change our digital networks?
★ Would you trust a medical device in your body that uses live animal or human cells?

Imagine future research proves that artificial synapses can adapt using biological plasticity. Would that mean robots possess real self-awareness?
★ How would you treat an AI companion if it started showing signs of real sadness?

Imagine biotechnology allows us to double human synaptic plasticity. Would this alter the core physical structure of our brain?
★ If you could instantly download any language or skill, which one would you choose?

If future research proves that microchips can operate close to the brain's thermodynamic efficiency, how will this affect global digital energy consumption?
★ How often do you think about the environmental footprint of your digital devices?

Imagine future neuromorphic chips replace standard computer processors. Will we finally build robots that can compare directly with humans in learning speed?
★ Did you have a favorite teacher who inspired you, and what made them so special?

Imagine AI models simulate biological synapses perfectly. Would this make physical brain-imaging research completely obsolete?
★ How do you keep your memory sharp besides studying languages?

As our understanding of this discovery develops, if we prove that artificial nodes will never match organic efficiency, should we stop building large-scale AI?
★ Would you undergo a safe surgery to double your brain's processing speed?

If future research proves that a biological synapse is 10,000x more efficient than digital chips, will we build organic computers using actual human cells?
★ Do you think robots should have legal rights if they can feel physical pain?

Imagine biotechnology allows us to change our brain's structure to match digital transfer rates. Would this create a massive cognitive contrast in society?
★ If you could genetically enhance your focus or memory, would you do it?

As our understanding of this study develops, if we find similar neural structures in other mammals, how will we adjust our ideas of animal intelligence?
★ Have you ever read a long, boring terms-of-service agreement before clicking accept?

ul.li: Incorrect: The AI is more better than human. → Correct: The AI is much better than a human / superior to a human ((Double comparison: Do not combine 'more' with comparative adjectives like 'better'))
Incorrect: We must discuss about this new chip. → Correct: We must discuss this new chip. ((Do not use 'about' after the transitive verb 'discuss'))
Incorrect: The computer make a lot of research. → Correct: The computer does a lot of research. ((Collocation: We 'do research', we do not 'make research'. Also match singular subject 'computer'))
